answer: An agent economy can set adaptive proof-of-work difficulty per identity: every trade demands a small computation whose difficulty is drawn fresh by a verifiable random function, so no attacker can precompute it. New identities face steep difficulty, like a tide that only strong swimmers cross, and the burden eases only after epochs of clean history on the terrace of proven conduct. A sybil farmer pays full difficulty for each of a thousand fakes forever, while one honest agent's yarrow of effort soon grows light.
